page: Microsoft Azure D8ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The system architecture is x86_64 and includes a substantial 480 MB L3 cache alongside 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is bundled with a 472 GB NVMe SSD, and it supports Premium Storage configurations. No GPUs are included in this instance type, and it does not come with complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate balanced performance characteristics across compute and memory operations. The Intel Xeon processor delivers strong single-threaded performance, as evidenced by a gzip compression rate of 35.05 GB/sec and a bzip3 decompression rate of 15.08 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% of tested systems. Multi-core stress-ng performance registers at 9302.94, while the Passmark CPU score reaches 16691.48. Memory bandwidth tests show a high read-only small block cached rate of 687.52 GB/sec, though this drops to 89.09 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, with large block writes performing at 39.04 GB/sec. The processor's Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instruction sets support specialized workloads, reflected in a strong text generation speed of 270.06 tokens/sec for a small 135M LLM model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D8ds_v7 offers a balanced resource density, combining dedicated high-frequency compute cores with local NVMe storage. This configuration avoids the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances while providing sufficient local high-speed disk space for IOPS-sensitive tasks. The instance is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, medium-scale database operations, static web serving (benchmarked at 16.54 GB/sec), Redis caching (achieving 15.0 million SET operations per second), and lightweight machine learning inference or data processing tasks that leverage Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets.
